Done — one execution, passed.

**Approach** (`out/T5/plan.yaml`): two inputs, `base::inputs/base` and `lora::inputs/lora/adapter_model.safetensors`. A single regex-capture `matmul` builds all 32 deltas at once (`from_a` = `lora_B` `[2048,16]`, `from_b` = `lora_A` `[16,2048]` → `[out, in]`, matching the base layout, so no transpose for `fan_in_fan_out = false`), `scale_` by `alpha/r = 2`, `add_` into `model.layers.<i>.<module>.weight`, then `delete` the scratch tensors.

The one design constraint that shaped everything: `output` writes exactly one alias, inferred from which alias the transforms write to. So the products are created *inside* the `base` alias as `merge_delta.<i>.<module>` — writing anything to `lora`, even a `delete`, would make the output alias ambiguous.

All four required checks are `assert` transforms (32 deltas via `count`, `not: exists .*lora_.*`, `shape [2048,2048]`, `count 114`), plus preflight shape/dtype checks.

**Verified independently:** 114 tensors, key set identical to the base, no `lora_`/intermediate names, all float32, 10 shards each ≤ 536,870,912 bytes of tensor data with a complete `weight_map`. The 32 merged weights match `base + 2·B@A` bit-exactly (relative Frobenius error 0), and all 82 other tensors are bit-identical to the base.

Report written to `out/T5/REPORT.md`.

One note on the task text: it describes `model.embed_tokens.weight` and `lm_head.weight` as tensors "larger than" 512 MiB stored alone, but at 412 MB (393 MiB) they are under the budget — the greedy packer is what leaves `embed_tokens` alone in shard 1, not the oversize rule.
